hook: Full sedan detail: the guess says $96. The math says $345
hook_say: Here is why pricing a full sedan detail from a $24 hourly guess misses by about $250.

rows.label: Hours on site, full detail, sedan
rows.why: A full sedan detail in the calculator's presets takes 4 hours on site for one person.

rows.label: Round-trip miles to the job
rows.why: Mobile means driving: a 20-mile round trip at 30 mph adds 40 minutes nobody pays for unless you price it, plus 76 cents a mile.

rows.label: Supplies per job
rows.why: Chemicals, towels and pads for one full detail: $20.

rows.label: The guess: $24.07 an hour x 4 hours
rows.why: Divide $52,000 of take-home pay by every hour worked in a year and you get $24.07. Times 4 hours, that prices the detail at $96, with no drive time, supplies, costs or tax.

rows.label: Break-even rate per paid hour
rows.why: Add self-employment tax, an estimated 12% income tax and $545 a month of business costs, then spread it over paid hours only, since only 65% of hours worked get billed: break-even is $54.80 an hour.

rows.label: Price floor, zero profit
rows.why: 4 hours on site plus 40 minutes of driving at $54.80, plus $15.20 of mileage and $20 of supplies: $291 just to break even.

fix.label: Quote with 15% profit
fix.why: Build in a 15% profit margin and round up to the next $5: $345 for the full sedan detail. The Price Sheet does this for every job type at once.

note: Example numbers from the calculator's presets. Yours go in the yellow cells.
